While this can be implemented efficiently via convex programming (see [ kothari_better_2017 , Section C] ), one has to take into account the outliers but also re-run the clustering procedure multiple times in order to avoid dependencies on the norm of the means. This directly implies the robust mean estimation algorithm [ kothari_better_2017 , Theorem 5.4, Algorithm 2] . To do this, one needs to keep a weight c i c_{i} to each of the points x i x_{i} in order to estimate more accurate means. The weight c i c_{i} essentially amounts for the failure of the convex relaxation to certify an upper bound on the “injective norm” and hence we have to downweight this point (e.g., it could be an outlier). In particular, one can show that the outlier removal algorithm of [ kothari_better_2017 ] downweights the bad points much more than the good points, when the “injective norm” is large. Moreover, they show that if the value of “injective norm” is small, then the returned points w 1 , … , w n w_{1},...,w_{n} form a clustering such that one of the clusters is centered close to the true mean μ \mu , which implies the robust mean estimation algorithm. A more complicated procedure is required for the list-decodable case [ kothari_better_2017 , Section 5.4] The above algorithms will be a crucial tool for our algorithm for recovering the FFD components.
